ideas.description: One systems change on the tip recipe (E007 commit 52204ad: 9 epochs, LS 0.2, cudnn.benchmark plus max-autotune-no-cudagraphs). Replace the final global adaptive_max_pool2d (and any other adaptive pool in the net) with an equivalent reduction, x.amax(dim=(2,3)), or F.max_pool2d with a fixed kernel equal to the spatial size. Its backward then becomes a dense masked/eq kernel that Inductor can fuse, instead of the atomic scatter kernel that took 0.48 ms/step (~2.5% of GPU time) in the E003 profile. The forward math is identical. Recompile and warm up in build() for the full batch, the partial batch and eval shapes. Nothing else changes.
ideas.expected: Time -1% to -2.5% (8.05-8.18 s vs 8.257 s). Mean accuracy within ±0.15 pp of 0.7542; only tie-breaking in the max gradient can differ. If time improves by less than 0.8% (inside timing jitter), drop pooling as a lever. If the change helps, re-profile and take the next-largest non-conv kernel.

ideas.description: Test the width claim in the direction that saves time. On the tip recipe (E007, 9 epochs), shrink the last block from 576 to 512 channels and keep everything else, head input included, consistent. Block 3 is roughly a third of the network's FLOPs (conv1 at 8x8 plus two convs at 4x4), so this cuts about 5-6% of FLOPs. Record per-epoch time and per-seed accuracy.
ideas.expected: Time -4% to -6% (about 7.8-7.95 s). Accuracy -0.2 to -0.5 pp (0.749-0.752), probably infeasible given the 0.12 pp margin. A drop >=0.3 pp supports H1.5.1: the 576-wide block is worth more than its ~5% time, so the next move is a wider last block (640) with fewer epochs. A drop <=0.15 pp refutes it, and 512 becomes the new base, possibly with +0.25 epoch.

ideas.description: Schedule shape (D001 flagged that the tree has no node for it). On the tip recipe (E007, 9 epochs), change only the lr schedule's warmup: halve the warmup fraction (for example from ~23% of steps to ~12%), keep the same peak lr 9, and decay linearly to exactly zero at the final step. If the base already decays to zero, change only the warmup fraction. The lookahead schedule stays tied to step count as before.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.05 to +0.3 pp at the same time (8.26 s ±1%). A gain >=0.2 pp creates slack to retry 8.5 epochs (E006 missed by 0.2 pp). A loss means the airbench warmup suits CIFAR-100 already; then try the opposite direction (longer warmup) once before dropping schedule shape.

ideas.description: Explore where capacity sits. On the tip recipe (E007, 9 epochs), cut the first block's depth from 3 convs to 2: drop one 128->128 3x3 conv at 16x16 and leave blocks 2 and 3 at depth 3. This removes about 6% of the FLOPs, the cheapest-per-accuracy capacity if H1.5 is right that the late layers matter most for a 100-way head. Dirac init, widths and everything else stay unchanged.
ideas.expected: Time -4% to -7% (about 7.7-7.95 s). Accuracy -0.1 to -0.4 pp. If the drop is <=0.15 pp, this is a better trade than an epoch: one epoch costs ~0.9 s and ~0.5 pp near the knee. It would then combine with the warmup or Muon gains to stay feasible. A drop >=0.4 pp means early depth matters, so keep depth 3.

structured_output.summary: The tip is E007: 0.7542 accuracy in 8.257 s at 9 epochs, only 0.12 pp above the 0.753 bar. Accuracy falls about 1 pp per epoch below 9 epochs, so trimming epochs is no longer possible without gaining accuracy first. The profile showed the step is GPU-bound in cuDNN and that conv kernel choice is already near-optimal, so the only systems lever left is a visible non-conv kernel. That is the new priority-4 idea: swap adaptive_max_pool2d for amax, because its atomic backward kernel takes ~2.5% of GPU time. I added two ideas that trade compute against accuracy: shrinking the last block to 512 (directly tests H1.5.1) and cutting block 1 to depth 2 (explore, H1.5). Each saves ~5-6% of FLOPs. I also added a schedule-shape idea (halve the warmup, decay to zero) to fill the gap D001 found, aiming to win back the margin needed to retry 8.5 epochs. I kept I012 (Muon at bs 1024, the main epoch-saving bet), I008 (progressive resizing) and I013 (proxy batch selection, explore). I006 (lookahead ablation) is still running. I dropped nothing: none of the queued ideas tests a settled hypothesis. The queue now has 7 queued ideas.
